lee: brief heads-up we pushed the 'adaptive-split' kernel to a canary fleet (3% traffic). initial signal: p50 -17%, p99 -9%, token cost -19%.

parker: great! what's the exact bench command and the baseline numbers?

lee: command: `tools/bench/run --profile=adaptive_hot --seq=prod --iters=4000 --warm=2m`

lee: tiny excerpt:
```
baseline: p50=60ms p95=145ms p99=210ms cost=1.00x
adaptive: p50=50ms p95=132ms p99=191ms cost=0.81x
impr: p50=-17% p99=-9% cost=-19%
```

nina: any uptick in error rates or increased retries?

lee: no error-rate spike in smoke. retries unchanged. mem +1.8% at peaks on a couple kernels but within limits.

parker: what's the fallback behavior?

lee: if frontiers observe sustained p99 regression >6% over 10m we switch to `fallback-kernel` and alert #runtime-canaries. automatic rollback path in place.

ci-bot: canary started by lee at 2000100000; targets=18 hosts; traffic=3%; monitor -> #runtime-canaries

nina: any model family differences? short-turn vs multi-turn?

lee: short-turns show largest latency wins. long multi-turns still get cost wins due to fewer KV evictions.

parker: plan to ramp?

lee: proposed ramp: 3% -> 10% (24h) -> 30% (48h) -> 100% with health gates. extra debug logging enabled at 10% for 48h. I'll open rollout ticket and attach traces: <https://internal.redwood/bench/2000100000>

nina: can you draft a one-liner for the weekly update?

lee: yes, will drop a 1-slide note. :tada:
